slides: Before you practice, here's a quick summary of the topic. How to read a definition, the types of questions, and the shortcuts.

slides.say: A new operation is just a definition. Read it, and then follow the whole rule. Whatever goes in takes the place of the letter, in every spot, and in brackets. Diamond of x is x squared minus five x. So diamond of negative two is negative two, squared, minus five times negative two. That's four plus ten, which is fourteen.

Read which input goes in which slot. a heart b is three times, in brackets, a plus b, so four heart two is three times six, eighteen. And the order can matter, so don't assume that two star five is five star two.
Inside a longer exercise, turn each operation into a number first. And nested operations go from the inside out. The inner result becomes the outer input, so don't stop halfway.
The operation works on an expression? Match the whole input first. F of four t is t plus three. For F of twenty, four t is twenty, so t is five, and the answer is five plus three, eight.
No definition? Put the input into each choice. An unknown input? Write the definition, and it's an ordinary equation.
Conditions? Check which rule to use at every step, because the input changes. Backwards? Try every rule, and keep an answer only if it fits the rule it came from.
Circular? Go down to the start value, then climb back up. The operation on both sides? Isolate it like an unknown.

Not always? One example where it fails is enough. Always? Swap the letters, or use algebra. Must be true? Plug in, but not equal values, and try a second number if two choices survive. And when the operation is in every choice, skip the question and come back to it at the end.
Two kinds of rules undo themselves, a number minus x, and a number over x. And an inverse operation undoes the steps in reverse order.

A value minus its value at the opposite number? The even powers cancel, and the odd powers double. And look for the shortcut formulas inside a definition. [pause] That's it. Now go practice, and I'll see you in the next video.
